correctness.rationale: A fresh reconstruction over all 81 ternary length-four words generated exactly 18,792 forbidden unordered triples, where one word lies in the descendant of the other two. The published 12-word witness contains no forbidden triple. After normalizing one selected word to 0000, the stabilizer and coordinate permutations reduce the second word to Hamming weights 1,2,3,4; exact include/exclude enumeration in all four canonical root cases found no 13-set. This exhausts the finite domain and establishes maximum 12.
risks: The proof is computer-assisted and parameter-specific, though the symmetry reduction and forbidden-triple criterion are complete.

originality.rationale: PASS. The directly relevant 2020 length-four frameproof paper was inspected in full accessible text: it prints the same 12-word ternary construction, but its sharpened upper theorem is restricted to odd q>10 and its conclusion does not claim ternary optimality. Chee–Zhang and the earlier/later length-four bounds likewise do not force 12 at q=3. Fresh Resultary search found no stronger exact ternary statement.

value.rationale: The ternary case is the smallest nonbinary instance of the length-four coalition-two extremal problem and is specifically highlighted by a later paper through a 12-word construction without matching optimality. Closing that concrete construction-to-upper-bound gap is a natural finite extremal benchmark, not an arbitrary slice.
